newsitem.title: USA: Time Warner to sell some cable systems - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Time Warner to sell some cable systems - newspaper.

text.p: Time Warner Inc., looking to shed some of its debt and nonstrategic operations, has offered to sell cable television systems valued at about $350 million, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday.

In Monday's electronic edition, the newspaper said the cable systems up for sale were in Louisiana, Mississippi, Tennessee and Michigan and serve about 150,000 of the cable giant's 12.4 million subscribers in the United States.
Time Warner has debt of about $17.2 billion.

The newspapers said the systems are not part of Time Warner's partnership with regional telephone company U S West. Instead, the cable systems for sale were originally part of Cablevision Industries Corp., a cable operator in Liberty, N.Y., which was acquired by Time Warner for $2.7 billion two years ago.
